text:
maya: heads up — i'm starting a merge of the customer's 'sparrow' LoRA into helix-3b@v2 to validate inference on their workloads. quick smoketest before canary.
chris: what quant profile are we validating? 4-bit gptq or awq?
rachel: target is 4bit-gptq first (to match their cost requirements). batch=8, seq=1024 for the quickpack.
maya: ran the first quickpack, noticed a regression on codegen unit tests — more hallucinations than baseline. sharing failing sample.
maya: ```
Input: "Write a unit test for function `sum_positive` that returns sum of positive ints"
Expected contains: "assert sum_positive([1,2,3]) == 6"
Generated: "The function should sum positive numbers, but be careful with negatives and None."  # missing concrete assertion
Test: pytest tests/test_codegen.py::test_unit_gen -> FAIL
``` 
chris: that's worrying. does same LoRA on fp16 pass?
rachel: yes — unquantized helix-3b + sparrow-lora passes the unit pack locally. so looks quantization + LoRA interaction.
maya: ran command: `./tools/run_quick_eval --pack sparrow_smoke --model helix-3b-v2 --lora artifacts/sparrow-lora.safetensors --quant 4bit-gptq` -> summarized results below.
maya: quick summary: codegen pass rate dropped from ~98% -> ~91%. p99 latency +25ms, median unchanged.
ton y: latency bump ok if within SLA but correctness regression is higher priority.
rachel: likely suspects: kv-cache alignment when merging adapter->quantized layout, or weight-ordering differences during merge/quantize.
chris: can you run a weight-diff check (L2) between: (1) float merged (merge_as_float), (2) quantized merged. compare per-layer norms.
maya: starting weight-diff. also trying `merge_as_float=True` fallback path then quantize after merge.
maya: command i used to merge: `python tools/merge_lora.py --base helix-3b-v2.safetensors --lora sparrow-lora.safetensors --out merged.safetensors --merge_as_float False`
rachel: try `--merge_as_float True` then `python tools/quantize.py --in merged_float.safetensors --out merged_4bit.safetensors --method gptq` — i've seen that fix ordering bugs before.
maya: quick local reproduce: with merge_as_float True then quantize, unit test pass rate went up to 96% in a quick run. still not as high as fp16 but much better.
chris: nice. let's document that as a recommended merge path for customers using 4-bit gptq.
maya: i'm going to update the quickpack to include: unit-gen, docstring-consistency, compile-check, and a small fuzz set for edge prompts. command: `./tools/run_quick_eval --pack sparrow_smoke_v2 --add compile-check,docstring --parallel 4`
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: helix-3b-v2 + sparrow-lora (merged_4bit.safetensors) -> cluster-dedicated-23, fallback=helix-3b-fp16
tony: if the customer is on Dedicated we should preemptively notify CS in case they see changed outputs.
rachel: i'll draft a short customer note explaining: we validated LoRA merges best when merging as float->quantize; can share mitigation steps. cc @tony
maya: update: quickpack finished. detailed metrics: codegen accuracy 91% -> after merge_as_float pipeline 96% -> fp16 baseline 99%. attached log link: https://internal/redwood/logs/1842004321/quickpack
chris: good. next steps: 1) standardize merge-as-float in the onboarding checklist 2) add a regression test in our eval harness that runs LoRA+4bit combos 3) update docs (devex) 4) push canary with fallback policy and monitor for 24h.
maya: implementing checklist changes now, will push PR for docs. tagging infra for longer canary: @chris please coordinate GPU slot on dedicated-23 for 24h.
deploy-bot: canary started on cluster-dedicated-23 (canary id: cny-1842004321). fallback to helix-3b-fp16 enabled.
ton y: thanks. i'll loop in customer success if we see any manual tickets.
rachel: small note — also look at tokenizer long-prefix handling in the quickpack prompts; different padding/truncation sometimes exposes quantization drift.
maya: noted, adding prompt normalization step to the pack.
chris: great work. once we have stable numbers, let's ship the onboarding note and recommend merge-as-float as default for gptq pipelines. :thumbsup:
maya: will follow up with PR and final results in this thread.
